prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Checkout A/B Test Results (language en).
Grid: 7 columns × 9 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "Metric" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Control" spans 2 col × 1 row; "Variant" spans 2 col × 1 row; "Lift" spans 1 col × 2 row; "p-value" spans 1 col × 2 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 13px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Metric" · longest unbreakable word 88px · one-line width 232px
  col 2: header "Control › Mean" · longest unbreakable word 44px · one-line width 46px
  col 3: header "Control › 95% CI" · longest unbreakable word 52px · one-line width 100px
  col 4: header "Variant › Mean" · longest unbreakable word 43px · one-line width 44px
  col 5: header "Variant › 95% CI" · longest unbreakable word 52px · one-line width 97px
  col 6: header "Lift" · longest unbreakable word 46px · one-line width 46px
  col 7: header "p-value" · longest unbreakable word 42px · one-line width 48px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 674px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 673px.
Fixed: content, font, 13px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Compare checkout metrics between control and variant, including estimated lift, uncertainty, and statistical significance.","reading":"Readers scan metric names down the first column, then compare the two means and confidence intervals across each row before checking lift and p-value. Wrapped labels should remain visually connected to their values.","groups":["Control and Variant each pair a mean with a 95% confidence interval; matching subcolumns support comparison between the two groups.","Lift and p-value summarize the comparison and should remain easy to scan alongside the group results."],"keep_intact":["Individual numbers, percentages, currency amounts, time values, and p-values.","Confidence interval ranges where possible, especially time and currency ranges.","Short column headers and metric identifiers such as 7-day and 1,000."],"may_wrap":["Long metric names at word boundaries, especially Support contacts per 1,000 sessions.","Confidence intervals at natural break points if space is prioritized for metric names; affected rows will become taller.","The two-level Control and Variant headers already occupy two header rows."]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r1A: widths [167, 67, 121, 65, 118, 67, 68] · table 674×400px · row heights [33, 33, 53, 33, 53, 53, 33, 53, 53] · column headers wrapped 1/9 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1B: widths [188, 67, 110, 65, 107, 67, 69] · table 674×380px · row heights [33, 33, 33, 53, 33, 53, 33, 53, 53] · column headers wrapped 0/9 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}

log.raw: {"critique":[{"design":"r1A","good":"Both confidence intervals stay on one line, making the Control and Variant estimates easy to compare.
